newsitem.title: TURKEY: Armenian and Azeri presidents meet in Istanbul.
newsitem.headline: Armenian and Azeri presidents meet in Istanbul.

text.p: The presidents of Armenia and Azerbaijan held talks at a conference of Black Sea countries in Istanbul on Monday following some of the worst fighting between the Caucasus neighbours in nearly three years.
Armenian President Levon Ter-Petrosyan told journalists afterwards that a fragile ceasefire between the two countries remained in place despite the recent fighting.
Ter-Petrosyan and Azeri President Haydar Aliyev arrived in Turkey earlier in the day to attend a meeting of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation forum.
The pair declined to comment on their talks.
The two countries traded accusations of cross-border attacks last week after two weeks of sporadic and violent clashes.

Europe's top security forum, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, said subsequently it would suspend its monitoring activities in the breakaway Nagorno-Karabakh region on the border between Azerbaijan and Armenia.
A ceasefire has been in place since 1994 in the enclave, subject of a nine-year dispute between the majority ethnic Armenian population, Armenia and Moslem Azerbaijan.
